LEAKAGE_CORRECTION_APPLIED.replacement: Eligibility is decided from record CONTENT plus the parsed target relation and identity.canonical only. Nothing else is read.

permitted: extract_target_relation(question) -- parsed from the question, verified equal to the oracle relation on 120/120 development tasks
identity.canonical / identity.surface from the I3 stage

LEAKAGE_CORRECTION_APPLIED.why: record_kind values in this corpus are generator answer-key labels: 'required', 'required_identity', 'required_current', 'direct_answer', 'dead_end_link', 'rejected_candidate', 'superseded', 'near_duplicate_*'. A runtime selector reading 'required' would be reading the answer key. No existing C4 selector touches evidence metadata -- s0/s2c/s2 receive only candidate ids and content text -- so using it would also be a new and undisclosed information channel.

RESOLVED_DECISION.decision: bridge_aware_anchor ADOPTED as S1's eligibility rule, by explicit owner choice, frozen before any arm ran.

frozen_fallback.EXACT_and_eligible: protect best eligible record, frozen S2c fills remaining slots

RESOLVED_DECISION.frozen_rule: eligible iff target_relation(question) matches candidate text AND (canonical subject appears in candidate OR candidate is anchored on an entity reachable by EXACTLY ONE runtime-visible hop from the canonical subject)
frozen_tie_break: direct subject anchor preferred over bridge anchor
RESOLVED_DECISION.one_hop_bound: Exactly one hop. subject->bridge->bridge->terminal is forbidden and asserted by test, because unbounded reachability is how this becomes graph search rather than a narrow repair.

superseded_open_decision.alternative_if_correction_is_rejected: Keep the original rule but restate S1's hypothesis honestly as covering UNBRIDGED EXACT tasks only (n=18 development, 5 defect cases), and expect no material aggregate movement. Then S2's connectivity constraint becomes the real primary hypothesis and should be promoted to S1's position in the ladder.
superseded_open_decision.issue: The eligibility rule as originally specified cannot fire on the population that carries the defect.

measured_fire_rate_on_development.consequence_if_frozen_as_written: A knowingly-underpowered arm on the majority of the defect -- the same failure mode as Sprint B1's R4, except foreseen in advance rather than discovered afterwards, which is what makes freezing it as-is the worse choice.
measured_fire_rate_on_development.correction_note: An earlier ad-hoc check reported 0% on bridged tasks. That check was WRONG: it evaluated the rule using the ORACLE canonical surface instead of identity.canonical from the I3 stage, which is the signal the rule would actually see at runtime. The committed script uses the runtime signal and is authoritative. Recording the error rather than quietly replacing the number.
measured_fire_rate_on_development.coverage_of_the_defect_population: The EXACT defect population is 39 cases on development, 34 of them bridged (87.2%). At a 21.4% bridged fire rate the rule reaches roughly 7 of those 34, plus about 5 unbridged: on the order of 12 of 39 defect cases, leaving most of the measured defect untouched.
measured_fire_rate_on_development.reason_for_the_gap: A bridged task's terminal-answer record is anchored on the BRIDGE entity, not the query subject. Worked example, ownership_chain-0000: question 'Which ownership tier applies to Sparrow intake manifold?', parsed relation 'ownership tier', terminal record '- updated Finch control module: ownership tier now 3529'. The record carries the relation and the bridge but never the query subject, so canonical_subject_match fails. The 21.4% that do fire are bridged tasks where the runtime canonical happens to appear in the terminal record anyway.

superseded_open_decision.originally_specified_rule: eligible iff canonical_subject_match AND target_relation_match AND record_kind is answer-support-compatible; tie-break fusion score then record_id

proposed_correction.name: bridge_aware_anchor
proposed_correction.relationship_to_S2: This makes the connectivity idea part of the PRIMARY hypothesis rather than an increment, because the defect lives in bridged tasks. Under the original ladder, S1 would be near-inert and S2 would carry the effect, which would misattribute the mechanism.
proposed_correction.rule: eligible iff target_relation_match AND (canonical_subject_match OR bridge_anchor_match), where bridge_anchor_match means the record's subject is an entity that appears as the TARGET of another candidate record whose subject matches the canonical query subject -- i.e. the record is reachable from the query subject in one hop through the candidate pool itself.
proposed_correction.why_it_stays_non_leaking: Reachability is computed over candidate-pool CONTENT via the existing V4 entity extractor, using only the parsed target relation and identity.canonical. It never reads proof_edges, latent_bridge, answer_node, required_evidence_ids, or record_kind.

superseded_open_decision.requires: explicit owner choice; no arm is run until this is resolved and frozen

S1.definition: S0 plus terminal-answer protection when identity_status == EXACT: reserve ONE packet slot for the highest-ranked eligible direct-answer record, then fill the remaining budget with unchanged S2c. If no eligible record exists, fall back to S0 behavior with no change at all.
S1.hypothesis: When identity is EXACT, protecting the strongest direct target-relation record before structural selection prevents S2c from displacing an answer the retriever already found.

S2.definition: S1 plus a connectivity constraint: every selected non-identity structural record must connect to the canonical query subject or to an already-selected bridge, else it is rejected and the slot goes to the next candidate.
S2.must_show: incremental value over S1, not parity

S3.definition: S2 plus temporal-current precedence: where two candidates describe the same subject and relation across time, prefer the currently-valid record. Precedence is read from record content, never from embedding similarity.
S3.must_show: incremental value over S2, not parity

S4.definition: oracle selector over the same candidate pool (existing C4_5 behavior)
S4.purpose: bounds what any selector could achieve on these pools

downstream_q.measured_on: Lightning A100-SXM4-80GB, commit 69ef0405dc4f895e27d45e7d584b9121bbcfb7fe, 5 arms x 120 tasks = 600 generations
downstream_q.note: Every arm's WORST family and WORST entity_regime delta is >= 0. No subgroup regressed at all on either monitored axis, so the two subgroup Q gates pass with margin rather than narrowly.

primary_criterion.metric: EXACT_bridged answer-support retention delta vs S0

protection_behavior.note: 35 of 54 protections used the BRIDGE anchor -- the population the original subject+relation rule could not reach at all. This is direct evidence the corrected rule was necessary rather than merely broader. The 17 protections that spent a slot on a non-required record are the cost of the intervention and are reported, not hidden.

development_results_2026_08_08.selection_only: No HRM. The PRIMARY frozen criterion is a selection property and needed no generation. Downstream Q remains a REQUIRED gate and is NOT yet measured.

fixed_conditions.corpus: development split only for construction; the consumed qualification split is never used to select or evaluate an arm
fixed_conditions.packet_budget_invariant: PROTECTED EVIDENCE CONSUMES ONE SLOT FROM THE SAME FIXED PACKET BUDGET. Packet size never increases. Without this, a gain could come from simply giving HRM more evidence rather than from better selection.

frozen_measurements: answer-support retention overall and split by EXACT / RESOLVED
canonical Q and abbreviation Q separately
packet size (must remain within the fixed packet budget)

REFRAMED_BY_PRE_FREEZE_MEASUREMENT.consistency_with_role_retention: Matches the earlier role-retention result: identity retention 1.000 and bridge retention 1.000 while answer-support retention is 0.529 (development) and 0.278 (qualification). S2c reliably assembles identity and bridge records and drops the terminal answer.
REFRAMED_BY_PRE_FREEZE_MEASUREMENT.finding: The defect is not 'EXACT identity' as such. It is EXACT AND BRIDGED. Measured on development, keep-rate of AVAILABLE required evidence:
REFRAMED_BY_PRE_FREEZE_MEASUREMENT.why_this_matters: RESOLVED+bridged is essentially healthy at 95%, so multi-hop structure alone is not the problem. The failure is concentrated specifically in EXACT+bridged at 12.8%. 34 of the 39 EXACT-identity drops on development (87.2%) are bridged tasks.

replicated_across_both_splits.canonical_below_baseline_on_qualificatio: canonical C4_4 Q 0.081 vs C4_0 0.190, i.e. -0.1090 -- S2c performs worse than no mechanism at all on canonical tasks
replicated_across_both_splits.definition: share of tasks whose required evidence WAS in the candidate pool and survived selection

c4_retrieval_fusion_v1.relationship: Every S-arm here uses R1 fusion, so candidate pools are IDENTICAL across S0-S4 and the only thing varying is selector treatment. Budget scaling (Sprint B3) is deliberately NOT combined.

c4_v2_1.relationship: Not reopened. The certified development bundle and the NOT_CERTIFIED qualification bundle stay immutable.

promotion_criteria_S1.family_safety: must not reduce any family Q by more than 0.05

promotion_criteria_S1.resolved_safety: must not reduce RESOLVED answer-support retention by more than 0.05

stop_rule.adoption_is_development_only: Any arm frozen here is a development-side mechanism decision. It is confirmed later on a FRESH untouched split, never on the consumed qualification split.
stop_rule.if_S1_fails: record descriptively, do not iterate variants inside this protocol
stop_rule.no_mechanism_edits_after_results_begin: Once S0-S4 start, no arm definition, eligibility rule, threshold or measurement may be changed. A defect discovered mid-run is recorded and addressed in a successor protocol.

FROZEN_OUTCOME.SELECTOR_VNEXT: S2 = bridge-aware terminal-answer protection for EXACT identity, plus the connectivity constraint
FROZEN_OUTCOME.development_only: This is a development-side mechanism decision. It must be confirmed on a FRESH untouched split, never on the consumed qualification split.
FROZEN_OUTCOME.headroom_left: S4 ceiling Q 0.7875 vs S2 0.5250 -- a further +0.2625 is available to some better selector on these same pools. Deliberately not pursued inside this protocol.
FROZEN_OUTCOME.justification: Only arm passing all 11 frozen gates, with genuine incremental value over S1 rather than parity, and it repairs the one structural regression S1 introduces.

S1.all_q_gates_pass: Q 0.4875 vs S0 0.3604 = +0.1271; worst family +0.0208; worst regime +0.0000
S1.cause: the packet-budget invariant working as designed: protection consumes one slot, frozen S2c gets 5 instead of 6, and sometimes drops a bridge record. The repair is large but not free.
S1.fails: structural bridge retention 0.575 vs S0 0.596 = -0.0212, outside the frozen -0.01 allowance
S1.status: PRIMARY HYPOTHESIS CONFIRMED (+0.5385 EXACT_bridged retention, LCB +0.3590) but the ARM IS NON-COMPLIANT on one frozen structural gate. Not promotable as-is.

S2.cost: RESOLVED answer retention -0.0344, inside the frozen -0.05 allowance.
S2.incremental_value_over_S1: Yes, on every axis the criteria care about: downstream Q +0.0375 (0.5250 vs 0.4875), bridge retention 0.660 vs 0.575 (it REPAIRS S1's only failure, landing +0.0639 above baseline), selected CES 0.583 vs 0.567. Identical primary effect. Not parity.

S3.note: This is why downstream Q was kept as a required gate rather than inferred from selection metrics: it is the only measurement that separated S3 from S2.
S3.reason: Fails the frozen increment requirement against S2: downstream Q 0.5125 vs S2 0.5250 = -0.0125. Selection-only metrics were identical to S2, so before Q was measured S3 looked like pure parity; with Q it is a small REGRESSION. Temporal-current precedence adds nothing on this corpus and costs a little. The simpler mechanism wins.

verdict_2026_08_08.bug_found_and_fixed_mid_analysis: select_s1 requested budget-1 records from the frozen selector then filtered out the protected record, silently returning budget-2 whenever the frozen selector had also chosen it. A packet SMALLER than the budget is its own violation of the fixed-budget invariant and would understate the arm. Fixed to request the full budget and drop the overlap; the ladder was re-run from scratch and selection numbers were unchanged -- verified, not assumed.
